name: OpenHands (Agent Canvas, CLI, Cloud, Software Agent SDK)
maker: OpenHands (company formerly All Hands AI; GitHub org All-Hands-AI now redirects to OpenHands)
summary: An open-source coding-agent platform: a Python SDK and Agent Server run the CodeAct-style OpenHands agent (or Claude Code, Codex, Gemini via ACP) in Docker, local-process or remote sandboxes, driven from a CLI, a self-hosted web control centre (Agent Canvas) or OpenHands Cloud.
status: active (main repo repositioned as 'Agent Canvas', beta badge)

first_release.d: repo created 2024-03-13 (launched as OpenDevin, an open Devin replica)

open.d: OpenHands/OpenHands LICENSE is MIT ('Copyright 2025 OpenHands contributors'); software-agent-sdk, OpenHands-CLI and automation are MIT too. 90,052 stars read 2026-10-05. Enterprise features are a paid product.

models.v: any LLM via LiteLLM, or OpenHands provider at cost
models.d: README: 'Bring your own model ... Use with any LLM'; docs say OpenHands uses LiteLLM for provider calls. Cloud: BYOK or OpenHands models at cost.

loop.v: CodeActAgent loop, task sub-agents, many sandboxes
loop.d: Default agent is CodeActAgent (skills default to agent 'CodeActAgent'). SDK Task Tool Set delegates to sub-agents that run synchronously; file-based sub-agents in Markdown. TaskTrackerTool keeps a task list. Agent Canvas runs one Docker container per conversation for concurrent agents and scheduled automations.

edit.v: FileEditorTool: view, create, str_replace, insert, undo_edit
edit.d: The SDK's FileEditorTool (str_replace_editor style) plus TerminalTool for shell.

context.d: General skills are always loaded (docs suggest generating an AGENTS.md); keyword-triggered skills, path-triggered rules, org and global skills from OpenHands/extensions. Default condenser LLMSummarizingCondenser summarises older events past max_size, keeping the first keep_first events and recent ones.

perms.v: Docker sandbox default; AlwaysConfirm / NeverConfirm / ConfirmRisky
perms.d: V1 'sandbox' providers: Docker (recommended), Process (no isolation, 'unsafe, but fast'), Remote. SDK confirmation policies AlwaysConfirm, NeverConfirm, ConfirmRisky with an LLMSecurityAnalyzer rating risk.

ext.v: MCP, hooks, plugins, Python SDK, REST API, ACP
ext.d: Plugins bundle skills, hooks, MCP servers, agents and commands (portable Agent Plugins format); lifecycle hooks in .openhands/hooks.json; Agent Server REST/WebSocket API; ACP for IDEs (Zed, JetBrains, VS Code).

where.v: CLI, local web GUI, Agent Canvas, Cloud, Slack/Jira/GitHub
where.d: CLI with headless mode for CI, IDE via ACP, self-hosted Agent Canvas with automations triggered by schedule or webhooks (Slack, GitHub, Linear), OpenHands Cloud, Enterprise in your VPC.

price.v: Open Source free; Cloud Individual free (BYOK or at-cost models); Enterprise custom
price.d: Pricing page read 2026-10-05: Local Open Source free; SaaS Individual free, 1 user, 10 max daily conversations, BYOK or OpenHands models at cost, Jira and Slack integrations; Enterprise custom (SaaS or self-hosted VPC, SAML/SSO, unlimited users).

notes: The flagship repo's README now headlines 'Agent Canvas: The self-hosted developer control center for coding agents and automations' that can 'Run OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or any ACP-compatible agent'. The agent itself lives in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk (V1). (https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands)

V1 docs rename 'runtime' to 'sandbox' and 'microagents' to 'skills'; the legacy RUNTIME=docker|process|remote variable still selects the provider. (https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/sandboxes/overview.md)
README warns about running the Agent Server 'Directly on your laptop (be careful!)'.

sources_read.what: licence, stars, created date, redirect from All-Hands-AI

name: Aider
maker: Paul Gauthier and contributors (Aider-AI on GitHub)
summary: A terminal pair-programming tool that sends the model a ranked map of your repository plus the files you add, asks it to reply in a text edit format (search/replace blocks, diffs or whole files), applies the edits and git-commits each change.
status: slowing: no PyPI release since 0.86.2 (2026-02-12) and no GitHub release since v0.86.0 (2025-08-09); last commit to main 2026-05-22

latest.v: 0.86.2 (PyPI); tag v0.86.3.dev; GitHub 'latest release' still v0.86.0

open.d: Apache-2.0 per repo metadata; 49,385 stars read 2026-10-05.

models.v: most LLMs via LiteLLM, BYO key
models.d: Docs: 'Aider can connect to most LLMs' (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama, OpenRouter, Copilot, Bedrock, Vertex, any OpenAI-compatible API); provider calls go through litellm (aider/llm.py).

loop.v: chat modes: code, ask, architect, help
loop.d: One request, one reply with edits, then lint/test feedback. Architect mode: 'An architect model will propose changes and an editor model will translate that proposal into specific file edits.' Ask mode never edits.

edit.v: edit formats whole, diff, diff-fenced, udiff, editor-diff, editor-whole
edit.d: No tool calls: the model writes edits as text. diff = SEARCH/REPLACE blocks; diff-fenced puts the path inside the fence (for Gemini); udiff is a simplified unified diff (for GPT-4 Turbo); whole returns full files; editor-* are lean variants for architect mode's editor. Force with --edit-format.

context.v: tree-sitter repo map ranked with PageRank; CONVENTIONS.md by /read
context.d: Repo map built with tree-sitter symbol extraction; files are graph nodes, dependency edges, ranked with networkx pagerank (personalised to chat files) to fit --map-tokens (default 1k). Conventions are a file you add read-only (aider --read CONVENTIONS.md), not an auto-loaded memory file.

perms.d: No sandbox. Every edit is auto-committed with a descriptive message, dirty files are committed first, and /undo reverts the last AI commit; --no-auto-commits, --no-dirty-commits, --no-git disable this.

ext.v: scripting via CLI and Python, IDE watch mode
ext.d: No MCP, hooks or plugins found in docs; docs cover scripting, 'Aider in your IDE' (watch files for AI comments), voice, browser UI.

where.v: terminal, IDE via file-watch comments, browser
where.d: Runs locally in a terminal; can watch files edited in any IDE for AI comments.

price.d: Open-source package from PyPI (aider-chat); no paid tier.

notes: Active-release check (2026-10-05): PyPI aider-chat 0.86.2 uploaded 2026-02-12; GitHub releases/latest is v0.86.0 from 2025-08-09; tags go up to v0.86.3.dev; last commits on main are 2026-05-22 (adding Claude model names). HISTORY.md main branch lists GPT-5.3/5.4 and Claude 4.6/4.7 support plus 'Aider wrote 62% of the code in this release'. So: maintained lightly, no release in about 8 months. (https://pypi.org/pypi/aider-chat/json, https://api.github.com/repos/Aider-AI/aider/commits, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aider-AI/aider/main/HISTORY.md)
The docs' 'Best models' list still names Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek R1/V3, Claude 3.7 Sonnet and o3, a sign the site is not kept current. (https://aider.chat/docs/llms.html)
Aider's design predates tool calling: the model writes edits as plain text in a named format, which is why the edit-format choice per model mattered so much on its leaderboards.

name: OpenCode
maker: Anomaly (the team formerly known as SST; repo sst/opencode now redirects to anomalyco/opencode)
summary: An open-source coding agent with a terminal UI (plus desktop app and IDE extension) that works with 75+ model providers, switches between a full-access build agent and a read-only plan agent, and feeds LSP diagnostics back to the model.

open.d: MIT per repo metadata; 211,882 stars read 2026-10-05 (site claims 950 contributors, 16M monthly developers).

models.v: 75+ providers via AI SDK and Models.dev, local models, subscriptions
models.d: BYO key via /connect; ChatGPT Plus/Pro, GitHub Copilot and GitLab Duo logins work; optional OpenCode Zen (curated pay-as-you-go models, some free) and OpenCode Go (open models subscription).

loop.v: build and plan agents (Tab), @general subagent, multi-session
loop.d: build is the default full-access agent; plan is read-only (denies edits, asks before bash). A general subagent (task tool) handles searches; todowrite keeps task lists; multiple sessions can run in parallel on one project.

edit.d: Docs: edit 'performs precise edits to files by replacing exact text matches'; write creates or overwrites; apply_patch also exists, all under the 'edit' permission.

context.d: /init writes AGENTS.md; falls back to CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and reads ~/.claude/skills. compaction.auto compacts when context is full (default true), optional prune of old tool outputs, reserved token buffer.

perms.v: allow / ask / deny per tool with wildcards; --auto
perms.d: Each permission resolves to allow, ask or deny, per tool and with wildcards (for example mymcp_*); --auto approves anything not explicitly denied. No OS sandbox is described in the docs read.

ext.v: MCP servers, JS/TS plugins with event hooks, custom agents and commands
ext.d: Plugins hook events such as tool.execute.before; MCP servers local or remote; client/server design (server port 4096).

where.v: TUI, desktop app (beta), IDE extension, GitHub Action
where.d: Mention /opencode or /oc in a GitHub issue or PR comment and it runs in your GitHub Actions runner, works in a new branch and opens a PR. Share links for sessions.

price.v: free tool; Zen pay-as-you-go; Go $10 or $40 per month
price.d: Read 2026-10-05: OpenCode itself free; Zen 'pay-as-you-go' per 1M tokens with some free models, card fees passed at cost; Go $10/month and Go Plus $40/month for open coding models; Enterprise link on site.

notes: Providers doc: 'There are plugins that allow you to use your Claude Pro/Max models with OpenCode. Anthropic explicitly prohibits this. Previous versions of OpenCode came bundled with these plugins but that is no longer the case as of 1.3.0.' It then lists ChatGPT Plus, GitHub Copilot and GitLab Duo as subscriptions that work with zero setup. (https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/)
Name history: sst/opencode redirects to anomalyco/opencode; the site footer reads '(c) 2026 Anomaly'. (https://api.github.com/repos/sst/opencode, https://opencode.ai/)

Charm's Crush (charmbracelet/crush, 28,499 stars, v0.97.1 on 2026-09-29) is a separate Go TUI agent; its licence is FSL-1.1-MIT (Functional Source License converting to MIT later), so source-available rather than OSI open source. (https://api.github.com/repos/charmbracelet/crush, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/charmbracelet/crush/main/LICENSE.md)

LSP: built-in language servers auto-install per language and their diagnostics are fed back to the agent; an lsp tool for definitions and references is experimental (OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL=true). (https://opencode.ai/docs/lsp/, https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/)

name: SWE-agent
maker: Princeton University and Stanford University researchers (SWE-agent org; John Yang, Carlos Jimenez, Kilian Lieret, Ofir Press and others)
summary: A research agent that takes a GitHub issue and tries to fix it, known for introducing the agent-computer interface (ACI): purpose-built commands for viewing, searching and editing files instead of raw shell, running inside Docker via SWE-ReX.
status: maintenance-only: superseded by mini-SWE-agent per its own docs and README

first_release.d: repo created 2024-04-02; paper at NeurIPS 2024; 1.0 announced Feb 2025

open.d: MIT per repo metadata; 20,491 stars read 2026-10-05.

models.d: README: 'enables your language model of choice (e.g. GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet 4)'. BYO key.

loop.v: one ReAct-style loop governed by a YAML file
loop.d: Single agent configured by one YAML file; history processors can rewrite what the model sees (the main reason the team still points people to it over mini).

edit.v: ACI tool bundles: windowed viewer, edit with linting, str_replace (edit_anthropic)
edit.d: Tool bundles include windowed (100-line file viewer with scroll and in-file search), windowed_edit_linting, windowed_edit_replace, windowed_edit_rewrite, edit_anthropic, search, filemap, submit. Edits that break syntax are rejected by a linter.

context.d: Context is kept small by the 100-line viewer, terse search output (just files with matches) and history processors; no memory file or compaction described.

perms.v: Docker via SWE-ReX, or remote (Modal, AWS)
perms.d: SWEEnv wraps SWE-ReX, which starts a local Docker container or a remote one on Modal or AWS and runs a shell session inside it with the ACI tools installed.

ext.v: tool bundles (folders with bin/ and config)
ext.d: Add tools as bundles: a folder with executables and a config.yaml; state commands feed prompt templates.

where.d: Runs from the command line on one issue, or in batch over benchmarks; EnIGMA mode for capture-the-flag security tasks (on 0.7).

notes: README warning (2026-10-05): 'Most of our current development effort is on mini-swe-agent, which has superseded SWE-agent ... Our general recommendation is to use mini-SWE-agent instead of SWE-agent going forward.' Docs: 'SWE-agent is now in maintenance-only mode.' (https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent, https://swe-agent.com/latest/background/aci/)

ACI findings in the team's words: a linter rejects syntactically broken edits; the file viewer 'works best when displaying just 100 lines in each turn'; directory search lists only files with matches because 'Showing the model more context about each match proved to be too confusing for the model'; empty output returns 'Your command ran successfully and did not produce any output.' (https://swe-agent.com/latest/background/aci/)
The arc teaches the idea: in 2024 hand-built interfaces mattered; by 2025 the same team found a bash-only, 100-line agent matched it as models improved. Last commit to main 2026-07-16 (fixes only).
SWE-ReX (SWE-agent/SWE-ReX, MIT, 616 stars): 'Sandboxed code execution for AI agents, locally or on the cloud. Massively parallel.' (https://api.github.com/repos/SWE-agent/SWE-ReX)

name: mini-SWE-agent
maker: SWE-agent team (Princeton and Stanford, the SWE-bench authors)
summary: A deliberately tiny coding agent (about 100 lines of Python for the agent class) whose only action is a bash command, used both as a terminal tool and as the reference scaffold for comparing models on SWE-bench.

first_release.d: v1.0.0 on GitHub releases (repo created 2025-06-28); v2.0.0 on 2026-02-11

open.d: MIT licence per GitHub repo metadata; 8,222 stars read 2026-10-05.

models.v: any model via litellm, OpenRouter, Portkey
models.d: README: 'Supports all models via litellm, openrouter, portkey'. Does not need the tool-calling interface, so 'you can run it with literally any model'. BYO key via env var or mini-extra config.

loop.d: README: 'Has a completely linear history: every step of the agent just appends to the messages and that's it', so trajectory equals the prompt. No subagents, no planner.

edit.v: no edit tool; files changed with shell commands
edit.d: README: 'Does not have any tools other than bash'. FAQ: actions are parsed from triple-backtick blocks rather than tool calls, and each runs as an independent subprocess.run, so cd and export do not persist between steps.

context.v: none beyond the linear message list
context.d: No memory file, repo map or compaction is described in the README; the whole history is sent each step. 'Great for debugging and fine-tuning.'

perms.d: README lists these environments. Because every action is a fresh subprocess, sandboxing is 'literally just switch out subprocess.run with docker exec'.

ext.d: Python classes (DefaultAgent, LitellmModel, LocalEnvironment) and YAML configuration files; a cookbook for extending. No MCP or hooks are described.

where.d: CLI for local use, batch inference over SWE-bench, a trajectory browser.

price.d: Open-source package from PyPI; no paid tier is mentioned.

notes: The README's own argument (https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent): 'SWE-agent jump-started the development of AI agents in 2024. Back then, we placed a lot of emphasis on tools and special interfaces for the agent. However, one year later, as LMs have become more capable, a lot of this is not needed at all to build a useful agent!' and 'This makes it perfect as a baseline system and for a system that puts the language model (rather than the agent scaffold) in the middle of our attention.'

On subprocess.run: 'every action is completely independent (as opposed to keeping a stateful shell session running). This makes it trivial to execute the actions in sandboxes (literally just switch out subprocess.run with docker exec) and to scale up effortlessly.' (https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent). The FAQ adds the cost: 'the agent cannot change directories or export environment variables; however environment variables can be set per-action' (https://mini-swe-agent.com/latest/faq/).

SWE-bench now exposes 'Bash Only' as a toggle on the main leaderboard, described as 'Show only runs in the mini-SWE-agent environment, so scores compare models rather than harnesses'. Best mini-SWE-agent runs on Verified read 2026-10-05: Claude 4.5 Opus 76.8% (mini 2.0.0, 2026-02-17, about $0.75 per instance), Gemini 3 Flash 75.8%, MiniMax M2.5 75.8% (about $0.07 per instance), Claude 4.6 Opus 75.6%. (https://www.swebench.com/)

README banners claim mini-swe-agent 'beats Claude Code and Codex on DeepSWE' and 'now powers Ramp SWE-Bench' (https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent). Its own advice: 'You should consider mini-swe-agent your default choice' over SWE-agent unless you want to experiment with tools or history processors.
The agent class file default.py is 190 lines as of 2026-10-05 (the 'about 100 lines' figure is the README's).

name: goose
maker: Created by Block; now a project of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation (repo block/goose redirects to aaif-goose/goose)
summary: A general-purpose open-source agent (desktop app, CLI and API, written in Rust) that runs on your machine and gets all its abilities, including file editing and shell, from MCP extensions, with shareable YAML 'recipes' for repeatable tasks.
status: active; moved from Block to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation

open.d: Apache-2.0 per repo metadata and README badge; 54,969 stars read 2026-10-05. Governance doc in repo.

models.v: 15+ providers, API keys or subscriptions via ACP
models.d: README: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock and more; 'Use API keys or your existing Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions via ACP'.

loop.v: one agent plus subagents and subrecipes
loop.d: goose can autonomously spawn subagents for 'process isolation and context preservation', including parallel tasks and subagents limited to certain extensions; subrecipes can run in parallel.

edit.d: The built-in Developer MCP extension provides shell, write (create or overwrite) and edit ('Replace exact text in files'), plus codebase analysis tools.

context.d: Looks for AGENTS.md and .goosehints at each directory level. Auto-compaction summarises older conversation at 80% of the token limit by default (GOOSE_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD), with fallback context strategies. A Memory extension stores facts across sessions.

perms.v: Completely Autonomous (default), Manual Approval, Smart Approval, Chat Only
perms.d: Four permission modes; Manual and Smart support per-tool permissions. Security extras: Adversary Mode (an independent reviewer agent watching tool calls) and prompt-injection detection. No OS sandbox found in docs.

ext.d: Every capability is an MCP extension (even the Developer tools). Recipes are YAML/JSON packages of instructions, parameters and extensions, shareable via deeplinks; custom distributions; ACP server for editors like Zed.

where.v: desktop (macOS, Linux, Windows), CLI, API, Zed via ACP
where.d: Runs on your machine; not code-only (research, writing, automation).

price.v: free; your provider key or subscription
price.d: Open source; no paid tier on the site.

notes: Verified: README says 'goose is part of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation' and the docs banner reads 'goose has moved to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)'. GitHub block/goose now redirects to aaif-goose/goose. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose, https://goose-docs.ai/)
Default permission mode is Completely Autonomous: 'Autonomous Mode is applied by default.' (https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/managing-tools/goose-permissions)
Adversary Mode is an unusual safety idea: 'An independent agent reviewer that silently watches tool calls to protect you in case the agent goes rogue.' (https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/security/)

name: Pi (pi coding agent)
maker: Mario Zechner (badlogic) and Earendil Inc. (repo moved from badlogic/pi-mono to earendil-works/pi)
summary: A minimal, open-source terminal coding agent whose model sees four tools by default (read, bash, edit, write) and which you extend by writing TypeScript extensions, skills and prompt templates rather than through built-in features.

first_release.d: repo created 2025-08-09 as badlogic/pi-mono; Pi 1.0 released 2026-10-01

open.d: MIT per repo metadata; 112,707 stars read 2026-10-05. New contributors' issues and PRs are auto-closed and reviewed daily.

models.v: 15+ providers, subscription OAuth or API key or local
models.d: Unified pi-ai package (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and more), Azure, Bedrock, Vertex, GitHub Copilot, llama.cpp. /login connects 'a subscription or API key'.

loop.v: one loop; no subagents or plan mode by design
loop.d: README: 'Pi ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub-agents and plan mode. Ask Pi to build what you want, or install a package that does it your way.' Sessions are a tree: /tree, /fork, /clone branch from any message.

edit.d: Default tools are read, bash, edit, write (grep, find, ls exist but are off by default). edit takes a list of exact replacements, each oldText unique in the original file and non-overlapping.

context.d: Loads AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md from the agent dir and project. Auto-compaction near the context limit summarises older messages (Goal, Constraints, Progress, Key Decisions, Next Steps, Critical Context, file lists) and keeps about 20k recent tokens; originals stay in the session tree. /compact [instructions] for manual.

perms.v: no permission system; YOLO by default
perms.d: README: 'Pi does not include a built-in permission system'; it 'does not ask before every tool call'. For boundaries: Gondolin extension (tools in a local Linux micro-VM), plain Docker, or OpenShell. Project trust only gates which project resources load. Extensions can block calls in a tool_call hook.

ext.v: TypeScript extensions, packages, MCP, RPC, SDK
ext.d: Extensions register tools, commands, providers, UI and event handlers (pi.on('tool_call') can block). Pi packages via npm or git. MCP over stdio or HTTP (pi mcp add), RPC over JSONL, TypeScript SDK.

where.d: Four modes: interactive, print/JSON, RPC, SDK. Slack/chat automation lives in the separate earendil-works/pi-chat repo. OpenClaw embeds Pi.

price.v: free; bring a subscription or key
price.d: Open source; uses your provider subscription, API key or local model. pi.dev links a 'Radius' product (used for /share) whose pricing was not checked.

notes: The repo badlogic/pi-mono now redirects to earendil-works/pi and the npm package is @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent; top contributors are badlogic (Mario Zechner, 3,836 commits) and mitsuhiko (843). Earendil Works describes itself as 'Bearer of Light', earendil.com. (https://api.github.com/repos/earendil-works/pi/contributors)
Pi 1.0 shipped 2026-10-01 'with Pi Durable' (a durable conversation, task and document runtime package). (https://pi.dev, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)

Pi now has built-in MCP support (pi mcp add, ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json), plus optional codemode and tool_search tools that keep MCP tools out of the prompt until needed; v1.0.4 added --no-mcp. (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md, https://pi.dev/changelog)
pi.dev: 'very token efficient due to its minimal system prompt'.

Arena, 'HarnessTax: How Much Does the Harness Matter for Coding Agents?' (16 Sep 2026, updated 18 Sep): 21 model-harness pairs (7 models x Claude Code, Codex CLI, Pi) on 30 tasks each from SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0, 3 runs per task, 100-turn cap. 'Pi reaches the Pareto frontier on both benchmarks by providing just four tools: read, write, edit, and bash.' Claude Fable 5 solved 97.8% in Claude Code, 96.7% in Codex, 96.7% in Pi, but Claude Code cost about twice Pi ($1.33 vs $0.67). (https://arena.ai/blog/coding-agents-harness-tax)

Same study: across shared models Claude Code cost about 2.0x Pi and 1.6x Codex on SWE-bench Lite and 1.5x Pi on Terminal-Bench 2.0, while the harness effect on success stayed within about 2% (Lite) and 5% (TB2). 'Across all seven models, Claude Code's mean initial context is over 10x Pi's.' GPT-5.6 Sol scored 83.3% in Pi vs 78.9% in Codex on Terminal-Bench 2.0 at about half the cost; an alternative harness beat the provider's own in nine of twelve comparisons. Caveat in the post: only two open-source benchmarks, possibly seen in training. (https://arena.ai/blog/coding-agents-harness-tax)

name: OpenClaw (formerly Clawdbot, then Moltbot)
maker: Peter Steinberger and community; stewarded by the OpenClaw Foundation, an independent 501(c)(3)
summary: An open-source personal AI assistant that runs as a local Gateway daemon on your own computer or server and talks to you through chat apps you already use (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, iMessage and 20+ more), with tools, skills, memory files and scheduled work.

first_release.d: repo created 2025-11-24; lore page dates Clawd from Nov 25, 2025

open.d: MIT per repo metadata; 391,456 stars read 2026-10-06. README: 'has no paid tier, hosted service, or token'.

models.v: hosted and local providers; harnesses (Claude, Codex, local) as plugins
models.d: README: 'Models and agent harnesses (Claude, Codex, local models) are plugins you can swap'. Provider plugins include API keys with rotation and OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex OAuth; an experimental agent-harness SDK replaces the embedded runner. README thanks Mario Zechner for pi.

loop.v: always-on gateway sessions, sub-agents, ACP agents
loop.d: The Gateway is the local control plane for sessions, tools, events and channels; agents can coordinate sub-agents or external harnesses via ACP and agent send.

edit.v: read, write, edit, apply_patch; exec for shell
edit.d: Files category tools are read, write, edit, apply_patch; runtime tools exec, process, terminal, code_execution.

context.v: MEMORY.md, USER.md, SOUL.md, daily notes; auto-compaction
context.d: Memory: USER.md (stable preferences), MEMORY.md (durable facts, distilled from daily notes). Older turns are compacted into a summary near the context limit, or by /compact. Skills are SKILL.md folders, shared on ClawHub.

perms.v: exec approvals deny / allowlist / ask / auto / full; DM pairing; sandbox off by default
perms.d: README: 'Tools run on the host for the main session unless you configure sandboxing.' Sandbox backends: Docker, Podman, SSH, OpenShell; the Gateway itself stays on the host. Unknown DM senders get a pairing code; group access is allowlisted.

ext.v: plugin SDK, skills, ClawHub, slash commands, HTTP tools API
ext.d: New capabilities 'usually belong in plugins built on the plugin SDK and shared through ClawHub'.

where.v: local daemon plus chat apps and companion apps
where.d: Channels: Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, Google Chat and 20+ more; native apps for macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, Linux; can be a shared team deployment on a server.

price.d: No paid tier or hosted service; funded by donors (Amazon, OpenAI, Red Hat, University of Michigan and others).

notes: Name history from the project's own lore page: it was Clawd in Clawdbot; 'In January 2026, Anthropic sent a polite email asking for a name change (trademark stuff)'; it became Molty in Moltbot on January 27, 2026, then 'On January 30, 2026, the lobster molted one more time into its final form: OpenClaw.' During the rename, bots sniped the @openclaw handle and Peter's personal GitHub handle. (https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/lore.md)
Governance: README says the Foundation 'employs the core team and signs releases' and 'OpenAI is a donor, not an owner.' (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw)

Security record: GitHub lists about 73 pages of published security advisories (10 per page, so roughly 720) from 2026-02-04 ('Unauthenticated Local RCE via WebSocket config.apply', High) to 2026-09-11; the 100 most recent fetched via API split 51 high, 44 medium, 5 low. Primary source only; press coverage of incidents was not checked (web search budget exhausted). (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories, https://api.github.com/repos/openclaw/openclaw/security-advisories)

Docs on the threat model: 'Treat inbound messages as untrusted input'; sandboxing 'is not a perfect security boundary, but it materially limits filesystem and process access when the model does something dumb.' (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw, https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/sandboxing.md)

name: Hermes Agent
summary: An open-source, always-on personal agent from Nous Research that you run on a laptop, a cheap VPS or serverless cloud and talk to from the terminal or chat apps, built around a learning loop that writes and improves its own skills and keeps persistent memory of you.

first_release.d: first tagged release v0.2.0 (tag v2026.3.12); GitHub repo created 2025-07-22

open.d: MIT per repo metadata; 251,476 stars read 2026-10-06.

models.v: Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, own endpoint and others
models.d: README: 'Use any model you want ... Switch with hermes model, no code changes, no lock-in.' Nous Portal offers 300+ models plus a Tool Gateway under one subscription.

loop.v: agent loop with delegate_task, todo, cron jobs
loop.d: Tools include todo, clarify, execute_code, delegate_task (subagent delegation) and cronjob for scheduled tasks delivered to a chat platform.

edit.d: Terminal and Files toolset: terminal, process, read_file, patch; write_file also exists; optional write sandbox and denylist.

context.v: .hermes.md / HERMES.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SOUL.md; memory; self-written skills
context.d: Context files: .hermes.md (highest), AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules; SOUL.md for persona. Persistent memory and session_search across sessions; /compress for context. Skills follow agentskills.io with progressive disclosure, and the agent creates and curates skills itself (skill_manage).

perms.v: approvals.mode smart | manual | off; --yolo; Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, Vercel Sandbox backends
perms.d: Eight-layer model: user authorization (allowlists, DM pairing), dangerous-command approval (smart default), write denylist, container isolation, MCP credential filtering, context-file prompt-injection scanning. Terminal backends: local, docker, ssh, singularity, modal, daytona, vercel_sandbox.

ext.v: MCP servers, skills, Skills Hub, 40+ tools
ext.d: MCP integration, toolsets, skills invocable as /<skill-name>.

where.d: Gateway for Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Email, Home Assistant; runs on a $5 VPS, GPU cluster or serverless; Android via Termux.

price.v: free; BYO keys or Nous Portal subscription
price.d: Open source. Nous Portal is an optional single subscription for models, hosted tools (web search, image generation, TTS, cloud browser) and cloud hosting; plan prices not read.

notes: Verified it exists: NousResearch/hermes-agent, tagline 'The agent that grows with you'; README calls it 'the only agent with a built-in learning loop: it creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, searches its own past conversations' (vendor claim). (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)

Direct competitor to OpenClaw: 'hermes claw migrate' imports SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, skills, command allowlist, messaging settings and API keys from ~/.openclaw. (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)
Docs recommend the SSH terminal backend 'for security: agent can't modify its own code'. (https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tools)
